summary: Taiwan manufacturing momentum remains strong and U.S. activity is still expansionary, but the macro backdrop is now materially constrained by a high geopolitical energy/shipping shock. Renewed U.S.-Iran escalation around the Strait of Hormuz has kept tanker traffic impaired and oil prices near six-week highs, raising inflation and rates risk for Taiwan equities. Russia-Ukraine remains a persistent secondary energy/supply risk, while U.S.-China semiconductor and tariff policy remains a structural risk for Taiwan technology supply chains.

geopolitical_global_risk.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran attacks involving tankers and vessels in/around the Strait of Hormuz have converted geopolitical tension into a direct commercial-shipping and energy-supply shock. Reuters reported Brent near $96.19/bbl and WTI near $91.03/bbl, with roughly 8% and 10% weekly gains respectively, while Kpler data cited by Reuters showed an average of 10 commodity ships per day through Hormuz over the prior 10 days, the lowest since May.

key_risks: Strait of Hormuz disruption and renewed U.S.-Iran attacks are a high-severity energy/shipping shock.
Higher oil and freight costs can re-accelerate inflation and reduce the probability/speed of monetary easing.
U.S. August PPI is due on 2026-09-10 and CPI on 2026-09-11, making the oil shock particularly relevant to rates expectations.
The FOMC meets on 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16 with a Summary of Economic Projections.
Russia-Ukraine remains a persistent energy/refined-products and European-demand risk.
U.S.-China semiconductor tariffs/export-control policy remains a structural market-access and capex-geography risk for Taiwan technology companies.
